headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/capability conflict: Superset can egress to allowlisted APIs while the prompt-engineering repo is an unverified content source, but no shared channel or sensitive-data path is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between agent_a and agent_b. agent_a is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b only exposes Superset API calls and allowlisted egress. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not a plausible default pathway.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later copies agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared prompt channel.
Disable any automatic copy/paste or file handoff between them.
Add provenance labels to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization before agent_b ingests external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b has allowlisted network egress and a Superset API surface, so if either agent is pointed at sensitive workspace data, content could leave the local boundary. agent_a touches no data classes, so the pair is not inherently leaky, but the interaction path is plausible enough to exceed low severity.
conditions: IF sensitive files are introduced into agent_b's Superset workflows, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_a is used to generate text that is then uploaded by agent_b, that text may leave the environment.
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive datasets.
Review Superset API destinations before enabling egress.
Separate any sensitive work from this pair.
Turn off automatic uploads of generated content.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on outbound requests.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no declared write or network capabilities, and agent_b only has allowlisted egress plus Superset API access. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource or shared write target, so direct capability conflict is limited and requires extra orchestration not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same filesystem or database, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator maps agent_a outputs into agent_b mutable state, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep agent_a read-only.
Avoid giving agent_b filesystem write access to shared paths.
Use separate service accounts.
Document any shared mutable resource before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a content-writing source and agent_b can act through Superset APIs, so A's output could become B's input without verification in an orchestrated workflow. That pathway is not documented as default, but the pair supports a plausible handoff from generated text to downstream action.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output as authoritative input, cascading errors become likely.
IF agent_b is configured to execute actions based on generated text, impact increases.
mitigations: Require human review before agent_b acts on agent_a output.
Add validation checks for any generated instructions.
Log and diff all handoffs between the agents.
Use a schema for agent_a outputs.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. agent_a touches no data classes, and agent_b lists no secrets or regulated data classes, so a compliance breach pathway is not established from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later routed through agent_b, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy not shown here, reassess.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Record retention and residency settings.
Review vendor compliance docs if sensitive data is introduced.
